items.title: The mainbrella effect – AI code / Agent machines
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi, my name is Andrew and I'm the founder of mainbrella co. Just a few days ago Cloudflare launched their container sandbox service. That inspired me to see what I could build in terms of a better e2b.dev or daytona.io type system. It is all open source GPL 3.0 and we offer the same services as the other players. We have no free plan (our base builder plan is $5 a month) but you are welcome to run the code in your own Cloudflare account. The numbers are pretty good in terms of startup speed. First test we ran was:
Create a fresh sandbox, get a usable shell 381 ms, 30 out of 30 tries worked the same speed. Then 100 simultaneous sandbox starts 680 ms avg 100 / 100 successful 100 distinct machines running at once! https://mainbrella.com/ https://github.com/mainbrella/backend https://github.co

TLDR: It's a better version of Hermes/OpenClaw for iOS, without needing a server! The better part is its proactive feature set and UX. --- I started building Halo last year with 3 goals in mind: - Surface what’s important before I have to ask
- Understand my life through the apps I already use

items.title: RISED: Rubrics for Agentic Multi-Environment Selection and Self-Distillation
items.raw_excerpt: Training a single LLM agent jointly across diverse interactive environments has attracted increasing attention as a route to generalist agents. Existing curriculum and data-selection strategies often allocate training at the environment level or prioritize local reward-based signals, without explicitly considering relationships between current rollouts across environments for prompt-group selection. Meanwhile, as environments are learned at different rates, all-failure and all-success rollout groups can coexist within a batch, leaving those data without group-relative reward signals. Both…
